findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (Senate roll call, 28-13)
findings.note: Voted aye on Second Reading of HB 958, Election Law Changes, as rewritten by the Senate Elections committee (Eighth Edition). The bill text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v8.pdf) says a county board processes a voter registration application only if it affirmatively indicates the applicant is a United States citizen. If the question is blank, the board sends a notice and a form and the applicant must give a statement under penalty of perjury within 30 days. The same text bars motor-vehicle office staff from proceeding with a registration unless the applicant affirmatively states citizenship. It also requires the State Board to set a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database, and sets weekly removal of deceased voters. The bill does not add a photo ID or documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement in the text reviewed. The same roll-call list shows aye on motions to table amendments 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, and aye on amendment 5. The bill was ratified 2026-08-06, vetoed 2026-08-17, and returned to the House (placed on calendar 2026-09-02).
subjects: removal of possible non-citizens from voter rolls

findings.motion: SB 1084 Reduce Early Voting Period, filed 5/18/2026 (named as a primary sponsor with two others)

Saved as a related election-law item, not as an ID item.
